static_traits.name: Li Bowen
static_traits.family_status: Divorced from former spouse, has two children; mother regarded by the family as the best baker
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends providing emotional support, but has not yet communicated with them about this issue
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar past psychological problems or treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, fairly logical and organized, good cooperation; emotions relatively stable (neutral attitude)

basic_info.main_problem: I feel inferior about baking, because I believe no one would want to try my pastries -- my mom is the best baker in the family.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of inferiority have begun to affect my self-esteem and the enjoyment of baking (it used to be my way of relieving stress); I hope through counseling to build a more balanced view and recover the pleasure of baking.
growth_experiences: The family has long regarded mother as the best baker; relatives and friends often highly praise mother's baking at family gatherings and use her as the comparison reference when talking about baking.
Divorced from former spouse and has two daughters.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / not as good as others.
My value depends on others' evaluations and comparison results.

special_situations.event: Bringing a self-made cake to family gatherings, where relatives and friends praise it while comparing it with mother's cake
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my work is not up to mother's standard, it means I am not good enough and not worthy of recognition
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids baking for others; instead practices doubly hard to prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never reach her level; no one will want to eat mine

special_situations.event: Hearing relatives and friends praise mother's baking and make comparisons
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Whenever others talk about mom's craft, it equals negating me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently seeking others' approval and evaluation to alleviate the sense of uncertainty
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I am not good enough

special_situations.event: When preparing to bake for others or to serve one's creations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by reaching the highest standard in the family will my baking be recognized; otherwise it will disappoint people
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Procrastinates or cancels baking for others; avoids inviting others to taste
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will not want to taste my pastries; I will disappoint them

special_situations.event: Received feedback from family and friends (including positive evaluations and comparisons)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as comparison exists, positive evaluations do not count; only with absolutely no comparison does it count as success
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring positive feedback, continuing to double practice to make up for 'inadequacy'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; I am actually no good

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen and to be affirmed and appreciated for his unique baking ability
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being compared, belittled, and not accepted, thus feeling shame and failure
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of being negated by avoiding showing one's work
Temporarily maintains self-esteem and a sense of safety by seeking external approval

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough learner / one who can never reach the standard
object_relations.object_representation: Nitpicking judges / impossible-to-satisfy comparers (mother, relatives and friends)

object_relations.self_representation: A child afraid of being negated
object_relations.object_representation: The image of a strong, near-perfect mother

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to express vulnerability to friends or close others and seek support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: They will think I am making a mountain out of a molehill and look down on me (projecting one's own worries onto others' intentions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone hesitant, repeatedly emphasizing 'this is nothing / I may be overthinking', avoiding deep exploration of specific emotions and details.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited in a session to recall positive feedback or acknowledge his own progress
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Positive feedback is not genuine or does not count; it is just comforting me
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using objective, evaluative statements, lowering the intensity of emotional expression, quickly returning to rational discussion of 'evidence/comparison'.

manifestations: Baking was once an important source of stress relief and pleasure; now, because of comparison, it has become a source of stress
Sense of self-worth is hijacked by external comparison, making it hard to gain meaning and satisfaction from the activity itself
outcomes: Avoiding showing work; relaxation and recovery functions in life affected

manifestations: Unwilling to share vulnerability with friends, worrying about being negated or seen as making a mountain out of a molehill
outcomes: Support system not yet effectively mobilized, maintaining the problem cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Worrying that one is making a mountain out of a molehill and daring not to seek help
Repeated self-doubt, daring not to express needs
Hoping to receive feedback of 'absolutely no comparison' before daring to believe in oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Presumes others will belittle or downplay her distress
Attributing one's own experience of being negated to others' evaluative intentions

positive_force: Has several friends who can provide emotional support (potentially available support resources)
Proactively seeks counseling, willing to try new perspectives and practices (change motivation and action)
Stable academic performance, with self-discipline and resilience
Still interested in and invested in baking, willing to practice and improve
negative_force: Excessive comparison and reliance on external recognition
Cognitive biases: catastrophizing, overgeneralization, predicting the future, and negating the positive
Avoiding baking for others, limiting behavioral attempts and accumulation of positive experiences
Shame and increased self-doubt, hindering the expression of vulnerability and help-seeking

antecedent: When preparing to bake for others or to serve one's creations
When hearing relatives and friends praise mother's baking and make comparisons
At family gatherings or when others expect to taste
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being compared and negated, with the internal core belief 'I am not good enough', and catastrophically predicting possible negative outcomes
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential experiences of shame and failure, lowering anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced sources of enjoyment and relaxation, impaired self-esteem, fewer skill-practice and positive-feedback opportunities

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly seeking external approval and engaging in self-doubt
antecedent: Receives feedback from others (including positive evaluations mixed with comparisons)
target_behavior.core_reason: Highly binds self-worth to others' evaluations, lacking internal evaluation standards and self-affirmation ability
target_behavior.function: Temporarily relieving uncertainty and anxiety by gaining affirmation
target_behavior.consequence: Increased dependence on external recognition, difficulty building inner confidence, maintaining the negative cycle
